node-1.label: Patient presented with dyspnea and fatigue

node-2.label: Patient is in their 70s and has no history of structural heart disease or hypertension

node-3.label: Medical history is significant for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma diagnosed 4 years ago, treated with 8 courses of chemotherapy

node-4.label: Physical examination showed blood pressure 96/54 mm Hg and heart rate 56 bpm

why.why: Both the pathologist and radiologist interpret the elevated NT-proBNP/troponin I, ECG P-wave/PR changes, and right atrial/pericardial hypermetabolic activity as signs of cardiac dysfunction, most plausibly due to recurrent lymphoma infiltration. The absence of structural heart disease or hypertension is only a minor refuting factor. Confidence is raised from 0.75 to 0.78.

Recurrent lymphoma is reinforced by the prior DLBCL and chemotherapy, and now by expert imaging interpretation of avid FDG uptake and right atrial/pericardial hypermetabolic activity; both experts regard recurrent cardiac lymphoma infiltration as clinically probable. Confidence raised from 0.70 to 0.74 pending histopathologic confirmation.

Pathologist and radiologist analyses explicitly state that anemia/marrow suppression is largely excluded and favor cardiac lymphoma infiltration; the patient's bradycardia is inconsistent with significant anemia-related compensation. Confidence lowered from 0.10 to 0.08.

Endocrine/metabolic disorder remains unsupported by laboratory findings, and expert analyses explicitly state anemia and endocrine/metabolic causes are largely excluded. The elevated cardiac biomarkers and imaging findings point to lymphoma infiltration. Confidence lowered from 0.15 to 0.12.

node-9.label: Laboratory tests show troponin I 0.04 and elevated NT-proBNP 3896.83

node-11.label: Echocardiography and PET show right atrial hypermetabolic masses

node-12.label: Cardiac lymphoma infiltration (lymphoma involving the heart)

why.why: Pathologist and radiologist independently conclude that the right atrial mass with avid FDG uptake, hypermetabolic right atrial/pericardial activity, ECG changes, and prior DLBCL/chemotherapy strongly indicate recurrent cardiac lymphoma infiltration. Confidence raised from 0.72 to 0.77, but remains below high because endomyocardial biopsy with immunohistochemistry, cardiac MRI, and restaging are still pending.

node-13.label: ECG shows prolonged P-wave and PR interval shortening

node-14.label: Endomyocardial biopsy and restaging are pending

node-15.label: Cardiac dysfunction due to cardiac lymphoma infiltration (recurrent DLBCL involving the heart)

why.why: The unified diagnosis of cardiac dysfunction due to recurrent DLBCL infiltrating the heart is corroborated by expert analyses describing avid FDG uptake and right atrial/pericardial hypermetabolic activity, with ECG/bradycardia findings consistent with lymphomatous infiltration. Confidence raised from 0.72 to 0.77; biopsy and restaging remain necessary for definitive confirmation.

node-16.label: Cardiac dysfunction due to chemotherapy-induced cardiomyopathy

why.why: Although 8 courses of chemotherapy are a relevant exposure, the expert consensus is that the right atrial/pericardial hypermetabolic masses and ECG changes are best explained by recurrent lymphoma infiltration rather than chemotherapy-induced cardiomyopathy. Confidence lowered from 0.15 to 0.12.

node-17.label: Cardiac dysfunction due to ischemic heart disease

attrs.why: Age is a risk factor, but there is no chest pain, typical ischemic ECG pattern, or structural heart disease in the graph; the observed ECG and imaging findings are better explained by cardiac lymphoma infiltration.

node-18.label: Cardiac dysfunction due to hypertensive heart disease

attrs.why: The graph explicitly records no history of hypertension and current blood pressure is low (96/54 mm Hg), directly refuting this refinement of cardiac dysfunction.

node-19.label: Cardiac dysfunction due to valvular heart disease

attrs.why: No valvular abnormality is described in the echo/PET findings; the right atrial hypermetabolic masses and prior DLBCL history point to lymphomatous infiltration rather than valvular disease.

node-20.label: PET-CT reveals avid FDG uptake in the right atrial mass and hypermetabolic right atrial/pericardial activity

node-21.label: Lymphomatous infiltration of the cardiac conduction system

attrs.why: The right atrial/pericardial FDG-avid disease, ECG evidence of prolonged P-wave and PR shortening, and bradycardia all point to lymphomatous involvement of the conduction system. This is a specific mechanism of the broader cardiac lymphoma infiltration, but biopsy confirmation is not yet available.

PET-CT shows hypermetabolic pericardial activity in the setting of known cardiac lymphoma and prior DLBCL, suggesting lymphoma has also involved the pericardium. Confidence is moderate because no pericardial effusion or thickening is described and histopathologic confirmation is pending.
